title: Pre-Analysis Round 2 — Thermo-Acoustic Blankets over the Aft Cargo Compartment Ceiling
abstract: Second round of pre-analysis for the aft cargo ceiling acoustic blanket, opened after the first round closed on the flammability question and left the lighting bracket, the smoke detection clearance and a cancelled predecessor unresolved.

sections.objective: Close the three questions the first round left open on the aft cargo ceiling blanket: the standoff bracket needed on aircraft already converted to solid state cargo lighting, the reduced ceiling clearance and its effect on the smoke detection sampling flow, and whether a cancelled predecessor left any released content that must be withdrawn.
sections.scope_note: The search covers ATA 25-50 as the primary chapter, ATA 26-10 because the compartment smoke detection sampling path runs in the ceiling void, and ATA 53-50 because the compartment floor and its repairs share the same access. The first round covered flammability and smoke penetration and is not repeated here. This modification was raised internally from a comfort survey campaign rather than from a customer order, so there is no originating internal order to work back from.
sections.method_note: Entity linking was re-run against the eight named aircraft rather than against a type applicability, because the modification is written as an MSN list and half of those aircraft have already been through a cabin refresh. Semantic similarity was run with two seed phrases about rear cabin noise and about cargo ceiling insulation. The most useful result came from the semantic side: a released air conditioning change with the same intent and no vocabulary in common was returned at high rank and had been missed entirely in the first round.
sections.findings_summary: Seven items were confirmed and one blocks. The blocking item is the cargo compartment lighting. Six of the eight named aircraft have been converted to solid state cargo lighting, whose light assembly mounts on the same latch that the thicker blanket displaces, and the deeper standoff bracket does not exist for the converted standard. The second important result is a released air conditioning change that pursues exactly the same objective by a different route: it re-tunes the air cycle machine to remove a tonal component from the rear cabin, where the candidate adds mass to block airborne transmission into the same rows. The two share nothing at all — no part, no zone, no chapter, no wording — and the first round did not surface it. If the acoustic target can be met by embodying the pack change on the four aircraft that do not have it, the blanket may not be needed on those aircraft at all. Beyond that, the lighting retrofit bulletin's parts list is affected, the parts figure and the lining installation task need re-issue, a cargo floor repair scheme shares the access, and a cancelled predecessor from 2017 left two withdrawn drawings that a search still returns.
sections.next_steps: Get the bracket question answered by the cabin systems owner: either a converted-standard standoff bracket is designed or the six converted aircraft are excluded. Model the acoustic result of the pack change alone on the four unconverted aircraft before committing to the blanket for them. Confirm with the smoke detection owner that a twenty-two millimetre clearance reduction does not affect the sampling flow. Confirm that the two withdrawn drawings from the cancelled predecessor are marked as such in the search index.

similarity_seeds: reduction of noise level in the rear cabin at cruise
insulation and lining over a cargo compartment ceiling

tasks.title: Re-run the entity search against the eight named aircraft
Re-run the similarity search with rear cabin noise seed phrases
Resolve the standoff bracket for solid state cargo lighting aircraft
Confirm the smoke detection sampling flow at reduced ceiling clearance

evidence.similarity_note: Both exist to lower the noise level experienced by passengers in the rearmost seat rows, and both were justified from cabin comfort survey scores. One speaks of a turbine silencer, a bearing cartridge and a tonal component; the other of a limp mass barrier, a lofted thermal layer and airborne transmission. They share no part number, no FIN, no zone and no ATA chapter, and neither references the other.

expected_findings.rationale: The two changes pursue the same objective by different physical routes and were raised by different departments five years apart. Four of the eight named aircraft have not had the air conditioning change, and modelling suggests that on those aircraft it would deliver most of the improvement the blanket is meant to give, at a fraction of the mass.
expected_findings.resolution: Model the pack change alone on the four unconverted aircraft and decide whether the blanket is still justified for them before the design is frozen.

expected_findings.rationale: The solid state lighting change mounts the cargo compartment light on the same lining latch that the thicker blanket displaces, and the deeper standoff bracket only exists for the fluorescent standard. Six of the eight named aircraft are already converted, so the modification as written cannot be embodied on them.
expected_findings.resolution: Design a standoff bracket for the converted lighting standard, or exclude the converted aircraft from the applicability and say so explicitly.

expected_findings.rationale: The lighting conversion bulletin lists the lining latch as a kit item at a fixed quantity and gives a single installation dimension. On an aircraft with the thicker blanket that dimension is wrong and the kit quantity does not include the deeper bracket, so an operator embodying the two in either order gets a kit shortfall.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-issue the bulletin material list with a blanket-standard variant, and state the embodiment order explicitly in both documents.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure already calls out the deeper standoff bracket on sheet 2 as a separate item for the upgraded blanket, but only against the fluorescent lighting standard. It needs a third combination for the converted lighting with the thicker blanket.
expected_findings.resolution: Extend sheet 2 with the third combination once the bracket is designed.

evidence.similarity_note: Returned by the description of work inside the aft cargo compartment with the lining removed, and by the shared phrase about compartment load limits. It shares no part number and no FIN with the candidate.

expected_findings.rationale: The floor panel repair caps the number of repairs allowed in one compartment before the load limits are revised. Several of the named aircraft are old freight-heavy airframes that already carry two or three such repairs, and the added blanket mass changes the compartment mass budget those limits are written against.
expected_findings.resolution: Check the repair count on the eight named aircraft and confirm with loads whether the compartment limits need restating.

evidence.similarity_note: The task's own note about inspecting the insulation blankets for wetness and displacement uses almost the same wording as the candidate's justification for replacing them.

expected_findings.rationale: The removal task tells the technician to inspect the exposed insulation and record the finding, but gives no criteria for the two-layer blanket, whose limp mass barrier cannot be assessed by the same visual check.
expected_findings.resolution: Add acceptance criteria for the two-layer blanket to the removal task at the same revision as the installation task.

evidence.similarity_note: Both describe work in the aft cargo compartment ceiling void affecting the airflow around the smoke detection sampling head, in comparable wording.

expected_findings.rationale: A cancelled proposal from 2017 covered the same compartment ceiling and its airflow analysis is still cited by later work. It was cancelled without embodiment but two drawings were released to issue before withdrawal, and a search still returns them.
expected_findings.resolution: Confirm that both drawings are marked withdrawn in the search index, and reuse the airflow analysis for the sampling flow question rather than repeating it.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned because it is a cabin change on an overlapping fleet that also adds mass aft and re-works ceiling structure, described in similar commercial language. It applies only to ZEPHYR-24 Evo aircraft, none of which appear in the eight-aircraft list, and it touches the passenger cabin ceiling rather than the cargo compartment ceiling.

Surfaced by the rear cabin noise seed phrase, and it is the fault isolation belonging to the air conditioning change that this analysis does treat as a genuine overlap. The procedure itself needs no change: it distinguishes the known turbine tone from a bearing defect and is unaffected by whether the cargo ceiling carries a blanket.

type_data.conclusion: Not yet issued. The standoff bracket for converted aircraft blocks six of the eight named airframes, and the overlap with the air conditioning change may remove the justification for the remaining four.
